semantic_changes: The trigger window grows from five seconds to thirty seconds while the state under test stays the boundary pair already used at the default batch size.
The control gets its own longer window, so the comparison is between a completed replay and a blocked one rather than between two five-second cutoffs.
Events are split into a case event before the attempt and a result event after it, so the admission record is separate from the outcome.

scope.description: Two cases on an in-memory commit-tracking store with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and the default MaxAppendEntries of 64: 8192 seeded entries, which is exactly 128 batches, watched for ten seconds, and 8193 entries, which is 129 batches, watched for thirty seconds. Each case starts NewRaft on a separate goroutine because a caller that observes no return cannot call Shutdown, and records whether the constructor returned, how long the observation lasted, the error, and whether a new goroutine was left inside processLogs.
assumptions: The control's completion time in this harness, a few milliseconds, is representative of how long a replay of 128 batches takes here, so a thirty-second window is thousands of times longer than a completed replay needs.
A constructor that has not returned within the window is treated as having made no progress; the harness does not claim to prove an infinite block, only that thirty seconds is not enough.
The seeded entries are ordinary command entries at term 1 with the staged commit index equal to the entry count and no snapshot.
excluded: No real cluster and no snapshot.
Only one longer window; the effect of the crash-recovery timeout between NewRaft and the caller is not exercised.
No attempt to interrupt or shut down the blocked node.

basis.prefix: For each case the harness seeds an InmemCommitTrackingStore with the entry count, stages the commit index to that count, and emits pp_case_<case> with the entries, the computed batch count, the batch size, the window length and the option flag. It then starts NewRaft on a goroutine with a fresh in-memory transport, a recording FSM and the default configuration plus RestoreCommittedLogs, and waits up to the case's window. On return it shuts the node down; on timeout it records that no return was observed and leaves the node alone. It emits pp_result_<case> with returned, elapsed_ms, error and the change in the number of goroutines whose stack contains processLogs.
basis.responsibility: A constructor that has not returned within a window thousands of times longer than a completed replay of the same shape needs is not merely slow; the caller cannot start, serve or shut the node down. The experiment measures whether the blocked case ever completes on a timescale far beyond the control's completion time.

comparisons.description: The 128-batch control must let the constructor return well inside its window.
One entry past the same boundary must still let the constructor return within thirty seconds; the harness records that it does not.
